trigger: Breach of security (unauthorized access to electronic personal information) of Florida residents. In this business: guarantor and applicant names with Social Security numbers or driver license numbers (SYS-06, SYS-07). Badge holder names, employers, and credential numbers are not listed elements; whether door access history counts as 'information regarding an individual's geolocation' (501.171(1)(g)1.a.(VII)) is a question for counsel
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable and without unreasonable delay, no later than 30 days after the determination of a breach or reason to believe a breach occurred. Record the determination date
notify: Each affected Florida resident, by mail or email; the notice gives the date or date range, the data involved, and a contact (501.171(4)(e))
applies_at_this_tier: Yes, if guarantor or applicant files were accessed (about 15 guarantors plus applicants since 2022). Building controls alone (schedules, setpoints) are not personal information

obligation: Florida notice to the Department of Legal Affairs
trigger: Breach affecting 500 or more individuals in Florida
deadline: No later than 30 days after the determination of the breach or reason to believe a breach occurred
notify: Florida Department of Legal Affairs (Attorney General), with the content listed in 501.171(3)(b)
applies_at_this_tier: No. The business holds personal information on far fewer than 500 people. Recheck the count in every incident

trigger: Good cause for delaying individual notice
deadline: 15 additional days for the individual notice only, if good cause is given to the Department in writing within 30 days after the determination. It never extends a Department notice

obligation: Florida notice to consumer reporting agencies
trigger: Notice required to more than 1,000 individuals at a single time
notify: All nationwide consumer reporting agencies (15 U.S.C. 1681a(p)): timing, distribution, and content of the notices

trigger: After an appropriate investigation and consultation with law enforcement, the owner reasonably determines the breach has not and will not likely result in identity theft or other financial harm
deadline: Written determination provided to the Department within 30 days after the determination; kept for at least 5 years
applies_at_this_tier: Only if counsel supports it. Unlikely when Social Security numbers were taken by a criminal group

trigger: A law enforcement agency determines that individual notice would interfere with a criminal investigation
deadline: Delay for the period in the agency's written request; the agency may extend or revoke it in writing
notify: Hold individual notices; keep the written request

obligation: Third-party agent breach notice to the owner (inbound)
trigger: A vendor that maintains, stores, or processes personal information for the owner (email and file provider, property management vendor, tenant screening service) has a breach
deadline: The vendor must notify the owner no later than 10 days after determining the breach; the owner then owes the 501.171(3) and (4) notices
applies_at_this_tier: Yes. The contractor security terms ask for 72 hours (POL-01 6.1)

citation: State breach notification statutes (all 50 states, DC, PR, USVI; Guam 9 GCA Ch. 48)
trigger: Affected guarantors or applicants who reside outside Florida
notify: Residents and regulators under each state's law
applies_at_this_tier: Check the residence of each affected person; guarantors may live in other states

citation: Business owner's policy, data compromise endorsement
deadline: Per policy terms; call the breach response hotline before hiring any firm so costs are covered
applies_at_this_tier: Yes. The endorsement covers notification costs and the hotline, not cyber extortion or funds-transfer fraud

citation: Owner's rule in this runbook; the leases have no data incident clause
trigger: Building access or climate control compromised or degraded; tenant employee credential data accessed
deadline: Same day for building safety; within 24 hours for credential data (owner's rule)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes. Not a legal breach duty for credential data, but tenants must know if doors or credentials were tampered with

obligation: OFAC sanctions check before any ransom payment
citation: OFAC Updated Advisory on Potential Sanctions Risks for Facilitating Ransomware Payments (Sept. 21, 2021); 31 CFR ch. V
deadline: Before any payment; full and timely reporting to law enforcement or CISA is a mitigating factor
notify: OFAC (license if a sanctioned party is involved); FBI or CISA
applies_at_this_tier: All U.S. persons. Strict liability for payments to sanctioned parties

obligation: Voluntary report to CISA and the FBI
citation: CISA CPG 2.0 goal 5.B (voluntary); no statute requires it for this business
trigger: Ransomware or takeover of a building control portal
deadline: As soon as practical; the runbook targets within 24 hours of declaration
notify: CISA (incident reporting on cisa.gov) and the FBI (IC3 online report)
applies_at_this_tier: Voluntary. Recommended: it supports OFAC mitigation and may bring help

obligation: CIRCIA incident and ransom payment reports
trigger: Covered cyber incident or ransom payment by a covered entity
deadline: Statute: 72 hours after reasonable belief of a covered incident; 24 hours after a ransom payment. Not in effect until the final rule is effective
applies_at_this_tier: No. Final rule not published as of 2026-09-25, and the business would not be covered under the NPRM's criteria (P03)

obligation: Payment card brand or acquirer notice
citation: PCI DSS v4.0.1 Req. 12.10.1; merchant agreement
applies_at_this_tier: No. The owner accepts no payment cards

trigger: Registrant determines a cybersecurity incident is material
deadline: Within four business days after the materiality determination

obligation: Covered telecommunications equipment or services discovered
trigger: Contractor identifies covered telecommunications equipment or services in use or delivered
deadline: Within 1 business day of identification (further report within 10 business days)
applies_at_this_tier: No. The business holds no federal contracts or subcontracts

trigger: Contractor identifies a covered article (Kaspersky Lab hardware, software, or services) in use or delivered
deadline: Within 3 business days of identification (further report within 10 business days)
applies_at_this_tier: No. The business holds no federal contracts or subcontracts
